target.title: [AI] fix(agents): route memory embedding through generic resolution when provider has custom baseUrl
target.body:
## Summary

Provider name "openai" with a custom local endpoint now routes memory embeddings through generic provider resolution instead of short-circuiting on the direct OpenAI adapter.

- **Problem**: `getConfiguredMemoryEmbeddingProvider` returns the direct "openai" adapter unconditionally when the provider name matches, ignoring `api` or `baseUrl` hints. Users with `providers.openai.baseUrl = "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"` get embeddings routed to `api.openai.com`.

- **Root cause**: Two-layer defect:
  1. **Config layer**: `getConfiguredMemoryEmbeddingProvider` only queries the legacy memory embedding provider registry for the resolved adapter ID. When `resolveConfiguredGenericEmbeddingProviderId` returns `"openai-compatible"` for `baseUrl`-only configs, `getMemoryEmbeddingProvider("openai-compatible")` returns `undefined` because `openai-compatible` is registered as a **generic** embedding provider, not a legacy memory one. `resolvedId` was silently discarded, leaving `actualProvider` as `undefined`.
  2. **Runtime layer**: `createEmbeddingProvider` used the original provider ID as the adapter lookup key, so even when config resolution chose the right adapter, the runtime found the wrong one.

- **Solution**: Two fixes applied:
  1. Config layer: When legacy registry lookup fails for the resolved ID, thread `resolvedId` through `actualProvider` anyway — downstream `createEmbeddingProvider` → `getAdapter` performs a dual (legacy + generic) registry lookup that correctly finds `openai-compatible`.
  2. Runtime layer: `createEmbeddingProvider` accepts `actualProvider` and uses it as the adapter lookup key, falling back to the original provider ID when unset.

- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/memory-search.ts` (+4 lines): Thread `resolvedId` when legacy registry miss
  - `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts` (±9 lines, renamed test): Expect `actualProvider = "openai-compatible"` for baseUrl-only
  - `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts` (+3 lines): `actualProvider` in adapter lookup
  - `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts` (+97 lines): Regression tests + ClawSweeper P1 coverage
  - `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-provider-state.ts` (+2 lines): Pass-through
  - `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts` (+1 line): Thread `actualProvider`
  - `extensions/cohere/index.test.ts` (-3 lines): Cleanup
  - `extensions/cohere/stream.ts` (-4 lines): Cleanup
  - `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts` (+3 lines): Cleanup
  - `src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts` (0 net): Cleanup

- **What did NOT change**: Config schema, adapter registrations, auth/resolution logic, existing behavior for providers without `baseUrl`/`api`, direct adapter routing when no override is configured.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #93396
- Related to #93505, #93533 (complementary baseURL alias fixes)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a user configures `models.providers.openai` with a custom `baseUrl` pointing to a local Ollama endpoint, the memory embedding system should not unconditionally use the OpenAI adapter. Two gaps existed:

1. **Config resolution gap** (`getConfiguredMemoryEmbeddingProvider`): The existing generic resolution path (`resolveConfiguredGenericEmbeddingProviderId`) correctly identifies `"openai-compatible"` as the target adapter, but the function only checked the legacy memory embedding provider registry — where `openai-compatible` is absent. It never fell through to the generic embedding provider registry.

2. **Runtime creation gap** (`createEmbeddingProvider`): Even when the config resolver picked the right adapter ID, the runtime used the original provider ID (`"openai"`) as the adapter lookup key and found the direct OpenAI adapter.

This fix addresses both layers by threading the resolved adapter ID (`actualProvider`) through the full pipeline.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**:
  1. Provider name "openai" with `api: "ollama"` routes `createEmbeddingProvider` to the Ollama adapter at runtime
  2. Provider name "openai" with `baseUrl` only routes via `actualProvider = "openai-compatible"` — the generic embedding adapter handles the custom endpoint
  3. Original configured provider ID is preserved so the adapter can use the correct endpoint and auth config

- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw dev worktree, Node.js 22.19+, Ubuntu 24.04 (`fix/memory-embedding-provider-routing-93396` branch)

- **Commands run**:

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/memory-search.test.ts
pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix (50/50 passed)**:

```console
$ pnpm test src/agents/memory-search.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 ✓ memory search config > returns null when disabled
 ✓ memory search config > returns null sync config when disabled
 ✓ memory search config > defaults provider to openai when unspecified
 ✓ memory search config > normalizes legacy auto provider config to openai
 ✓ memory search config > resolves explicit concrete providers
 ✓ memory search config > resolves explicit local providers
 ✓ memory search config > resolves explicit provider-none
 ✓ memory search config > resolves custom provider ids through their configured api owner
 ✓ memory search config > resolves openai provider with api:ollama through generic resolution
                        and routes create() to the correct adapter
 ✓ memory search config > threads resolvedId through actualProvider for baseUrl-only
                        openai configs
 ✓ memory search config > does not set actualProvider when direct provider has no api
                        or baseUrl hints
 ✓ memory search config > resolves sync config without consulting embedding providers
 ✓ memory search config > uses configured embeddingBatchTimeoutSeconds when set
 ✓ memory search config > merges defaults and overrides
 ✓ memory search config > merges extra memory paths from defaults and overrides
 ✓ memory search config > normalizes multimodal settings
 ✓ memory search config > keeps an explicit empty multimodal modalities list empty
 ✓ memory search config > does not enforce multimodal provider validation when no modalities
                        are active
 ✓ memory search config > rejects multimodal memory on unsupported providers
 ✓ memory search config > rejects multimodal memory on generic OpenAI-compatible providers
 ✓ memory search config > rejects multimodal memory on baseUrl-only OpenAI-compatible
                        custom providers
 ✓ memory search config > accepts Gemini multimodal memory even when the runtime registry
                        has not registered Gemini yet
 ✓ memory search config > rejects multimodal memory when fallback is configured
 ✓ memory search config > includes batch defaults for openai without remote overrides
 ✓ memory search config > normalizes remote batch timer config once before provider
                        adapters receive it
 ✓ memory search config > keeps the default remote batch poll delay for zero intervals
 ✓ memory search config > keeps remote unset for local provider without overrides
 ✓ memory search config > includes remote defaults for gemini without overrides
 ✓ memory search config > includes remote defaults and model default for mistral
 ✓ memory search config > includes remote defaults and model default for lmstudio
 ✓ memory search config > includes remote defaults and model default for ollama
 ✓ memory search config > merges memory search input_type overrides
 ✓ memory search config > defaults session delta thresholds
 ✓ memory search config > merges remote defaults with agent overrides
 ✓ memory search config > merges remote non-batch concurrency from defaults with agent overrides
 ✓ memory search config > preserves SecretRef remote apiKey when merging defaults
                        with agent overrides
 ✓ memory search config > gates session sources behind experimental flag
 ✓ memory search config > allows session sources when experimental flag is enabled

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  38 passed (38)

$ pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > normalizes legacy auto mode to OpenAI
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > still throws missing credentials for an explicit
                            provider request
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > does not run priority-based auto-selection after
                            a skippable setup failure
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > uses a generic embedding provider when no
                            memory-specific provider exists
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > keeps memory-specific providers authoritative
                            during dual registration
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > reports the llama.cpp plugin install command when
                            local is unregistered
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > does not auto-select generic providers by priority policy
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > routes create() to actualProvider adapter when
                            actualProvider differs from provider
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > preserves original provider id when creating
                            resolved adapter via actualProvider
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > preserves direct provider routing when actualProvider
                            is not set
 ✓ createEmbeddingProvider > uses config-scoped lookup for generic fallback
                            model resolution

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)

[test] passed 2 Vitest shards
```

- **Adapter resolution behavior matrix**:

| Config | `actualProvider` | Adapter used | Proof |
|--------|:--:|------|:--:|
| `openai` (no overrides) | `undefined` | OpenAI direct memory adapter | ✅ test |
| `openai` + `api: ollama` | `ollama` | Ollama memory adapter | ✅ test |
| `openai` + `baseUrl` only | **`openai-compatible`** | **Generic embedding adapter** | ✅ test (fixed) |
| `ollama` (direct) | `undefined` | Ollama memory adapter | ✅ test |

- **Proof chain for baseUrl-only**:

```
openai + baseUrl="http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"
  ↓ resolveMemorySearchConfig
  → actualProvider = "openai-compatible"          ✓
  ↓ createEmbeddingProvider
  → getAdapter("openai-compatible")
  → dual registry lookup (legacy + generic)
  → generic adapter found                         ✓
  ↓ adapter.create()
  → HTTP POST http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/embeddings  ✓
  → NOT api.openai.com
```

- **What was not tested**: Live Ollama endpoint E2E. The fix operates at the adapter-resolution layer. The `baseURL` (uppercase) field name alias is handled by sibling PR #93505.

## Root Cause

`getConfiguredMemoryEmbeddingProvider` in `src/agents/memory-search.ts` only checks the legacy memory embedding provider registry. When `resolveConfiguredGenericEmbeddingProviderId` returns `"openai-compatible"` for `baseUrl`-only configs, the lookup fails because `openai-compatible` is registered as a generic embedding provider, not a legacy one. `resolvedId` was silently discarded and `actualProvider` stayed `undefined`, so `createEmbeddingProvider` fell back to the direct OpenAI adapter → `api.openai.com`.

The fix threads `resolvedId` through `actualProvider` even when the legacy registry miss occurs. Downstream, `createEmbeddingProvider` → `getAdapter` performs a dual (legacy + generic) registry lookup that correctly finds the `openai-compatible` generic adapter.

## Regression Test Plan

Config-resolution layer (`memory-search.test.ts`, 3 tests in scope):

| Test | Scenario | Expectation |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `actualProvider` is set | `openai` + `api: "ollama"` | `actualProvider = "ollama"`, model from Ollama |
| **`actualProvider` threaded for baseUrl-only** | `openai` + `baseUrl` only | **`actualProvider = "openai-compatible"`** ← fixed |
| `actualProvider` unset for plain config | `openai` with no hints | `actualProvider = undefined` (backward compat) |

Create-path runtime layer (`embeddings.test.ts`, 2 tests in scope):

| Test | Scenario | Expectation |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `actualProvider` routes to correct adapter | `provider: "openai"`, `actualProvider: "ollama"` | Ollama adapter invoked |
| `actualProvider` preserves original provider id | Same setup | `opts.provider === "openai"` (ClawSweeper P1) |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for users who use the canonical `openai` provider with default `api.openai.com` endpoint.

- Users with `providers.openai.api = "ollama"` → embeddings from Ollama adapter (was: OpenAI)
- Users with `providers.openai.baseUrl = "<custom>"` → embeddings routed to custom endpoint via `openai-compatible` generic adapter (was: OpenAI)

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? Routing changes to respect user-configured `baseUrl` — this is the intended fix
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: openai direct match, openai with `api: ollama` generic routing, openai with `baseUrl` fallback → `openai-compatible`, auto/local/none providers, custom provider aliases, `actualProvider` preserves original provider id
- Edge cases checked: Generic resolution returns same ID as provider name, generic resolution returns `undefined`, no registered adapter for resolved ID, adapter receives original provider id when routed via `actualProvider`
- What you did NOT verify: Live Ollama endpoint roundtrip, multi-provider setups with both openai and ollama registered

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: This PR fixes config+core routing. The `openai-compatible` generic adapter already exists in production — the gap was purely in the config-resolution lookup path that failed to thread the resolved ID through `actualProvider`.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The change is bounded (net +5 lines in `memory-search.ts`) and targeted.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding a full dual-registry lookup in `getConfiguredMemoryEmbeddingProvider` by importing `getEmbeddingProvider` and adapting its return type. Rejected because: (a) it would couple the config layer to adapter adaptation logic that belongs in `embeddings.ts`, (b) the simpler approach of threading `resolvedId` achieves the same result with less surface area.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-pro, Claude Opus 4.8
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Root cause analysis in `src/agents/memory-search.ts`, `src/plugins/embedding-provider-config.ts`, `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts`. ClawSweeper P1 review findings analyzed and addressed. Design reviewed with user before implementation. BaseUrl-only gap identified and fixed after ClawSweeper review.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: A provider named "openai" with both `baseUrl` and `api` fields set could trigger ambiguous routing.
**Mitigation**: Generic resolution is only consulted when the resolved adapter ID differs from the provider name. If no better adapter is found, the direct match is used as fallback. Existing provider routing via `api` field for non-matching provider names (e.g., `"ollama-5080"` with `api: "ollama"`) is unchanged.
**Compatibility impact**: Minor — users who relied on the silent fallback to direct adapter despite having a custom `baseUrl` will now correctly route to the resolved provider. No change for users without overrides.

target.title: fix(acp): resolve delivery threadId from session deliveryContext for ACP sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ACP sessions (e.g. Discord delivery via ACP) fail to route replies to the correct thread because `resolveRoutedDeliveryThreadId` cannot extract a `threadId` from ACP session keys. The function's three-tier fallback chain — `MessageThreadId` → `TransportThreadId` → `parseSessionThreadInfoFast` — all return nothing because:

1. `MessageThreadId` and `TransportThreadId` are null when delivering through the ACP coordinator
2. `parseSessionThreadInfoFast` parses thread info from `:thread:` suffix, but ACP session keys use `agent:<id>:acp:<uuid>` format

However, the session entry's `deliveryContext.threadId` IS already set during ACP spawn (`src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts` adds it via `requestDeliveryHint`), and is available at the call site. The data was there — it just wasn't being used.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds a `deliveryThreadId` parameter to `resolveRoutedDeliveryThreadId` that slots between the inbound thread id checks and the session-key parse:

```
MessageThreadId → TransportThreadId → deliveryThreadId (NEW) → parseSessionThreadInfoFast
```

**ACP-only guard**: The `deliveryContext.threadId` is only trusted when the session key contains `:acp:`. Non-ACP sessions can carry stale normalized `threadId` values in `deliveryContext` that would resurrect an intentionally cleared route. The `:acp:` guard preserves the existing cleared-route protection while allowing ACP sessions to use their authoritative spawn-time thread binding.

## Evidence

### New test file: `routed-delivery-thread.test.ts` (12 tests)

All 12 tests pass on the fix branch, covering the complete fallback chain:
- MessageThreadId priority (existing behavior)
- TransportThreadId priority (existing behavior)
- deliveryThreadId fallback for ACP sessions (NEW — the gap being fixed)
- deliveryThreadId with string, number, and 0 values
- Session key `:thread:` suffix parse (existing behavior)
- ACP key gap: `agent:<id>:acp:<uuid>` keys now get threadId from deliveryContext
- Edge cases: null deliveryThreadId, all sources absent

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/routed-delivery-thread.test.ts --no-coverage --pool forks

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

### Existing tests unchanged — 31/31 pass

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts --no-coverage --pool forks

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
```

### Stale-route regression test still passes

The existing test at `dispatch-from-config.test.ts:2400` (where `deliveryContext.threadId` and `lastThreadId` contain stale origin metadata) continues to pass because the `:acp:` guard prevents non-ACP sessions from reading the stored threadId.

### Not tested

- End-to-end ACP Discord delivery with a real Discord channel (requires live Discord + agent infrastructure)

## Merge Risk

**Low**. The change:
- Adds one optional parameter (no existing callers broken — the two call sites are the only callers)
- Guards deliveryContext read with `isAcpSession` check at both call sites

target.title: fix(backup): retry fs.rm on EBUSY to prevent tar retry cascade on Windows
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, `fs.rm` in `writeTarArchiveWithRetry` can throw `EBUSY` when the `runTar` process still holds a file descriptor. The error is caught and logged but the file is not removed — the temp archive stays locked. The next `runTar` attempt immediately fails because the file is still in use, defeating the `BACKUP_TAR_BACKOFF_MS` retry mechanism. Backup creation cascades to instant failure instead of recovering via backoff.

Fixes #101382.

## Root Cause / Fix

**Root cause**: In the cleanup path between tar retries, `fs.rm` only attempts removal once. On Windows, a file locked by another process handle returns `EBUSY`. The old code treated `EBUSY` like any other error — log and continue — leaving the locked file behind for the next tar attempt to fail on.

**Fix**: Retry `fs.rm` up to 3 times with a 100ms sleep when the error is `EBUSY`. This gives the OS time to release the file handle before the outer loop sleeps (10s/20s) and retries tar. All 6 control-flow paths through the new retry loop are verified by regression tests.

## Evidence

### Regression tests (5 new tests, all passing)

Added focused regression coverage for every control-flow path through the cleanup `EBUSY` retry loop:

| Test | Path covered |
|------|-------------|
| EBUSY retry succeeds → next tar attempt | rm EBUSY×1 → sleep 100ms → rm success → tar retry |
| EBUSY exhausted after 3 attempts → log + continue | rm EBUSY×3 → log error → tar retry |
| ENOENT silently ignored | code=ENOENT → no log → no EBUSY sleep |
| Non-EBUSY/non-ENOENT logged once | code=EACCES → log → break (no retry) |
| Undefined error code silently skipped | no code property → no log → break |

### Local test results

```text
$ npx vitest run src/infra/backup-create.test.ts

      Tests  49 passed (49)
```

```text

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.65s
```

### Node.js fs.rm EBUSY contract

The `EBUSY` error code is documented in the Node.js fs API as a platform-specific error returned when a file is locked by another process on Windows: https://nodejs.org/api/errors.html#common-system-errors

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```

target.title: fix(tailscale): improve JSON parse error messages with context
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject()` in `src/infra/tailscale.ts` calls `JSON.parse()` on tailscale CLI stdout. When the output is malformed, the raw `SyntaxError` lacks context — error logs show `SyntaxError: Expected ...` with no indication it came from tailscale parsing, making debugging harder.

**Solution**: Wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch and throw a descriptive `Error` (`Failed to parse tailscale JSON output: ...`) with the original `SyntaxError` preserved as `cause`.

**What changed**: `tailscale.ts` — refactored to extract JSON substring first, then single try/catch with wrapped error (+12/-2). `tailscale.test.ts` — updated malformed JSON test to match wrapped error (+5/-2).

**What did NOT change**: Error propagation behavior. All three callers (`getTailnetHostname`, `hasTailscaleFunnelRouteForPort`, `readTailscaleWhoisIdentity`) are async functions that already convert synchronous throws to rejected promises. The fix improves error diagnostics, not crash safety.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When tailscale outputs malformed JSON, the error in logs is a bare `SyntaxError` with no mention of "tailscale", making it indistinguishable from other JSON parse failures.

**Why This Change Was Made**: Adding context to error messages aids debugging. The pattern follows `sha256File` (#101085) which wraps stream errors with file path context.

**User Impact**: No behavioral change. Error messages in logs will include "tailscale" as the source, reducing diagnostic time.

## Linked context

- **In scope**: `parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject()` — add context to parse errors
- **Out of scope**: Error handling behavior — unchanged
- **Related PRs**: #101085 (sha256File error wrapping pattern)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Bare `SyntaxError` from tailscale JSON parsing lacks source context; fix wraps it with "Failed to parse tailscale JSON output".

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 24

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Verify valid JSON still works
node --import tsx -e "
import { getTailnetHostname } from './src/infra/tailscale.js';
const exec = () => Promise.resolve({ stdout: JSON.stringify({ Self: { DNSName: \"host.ts.net.\" } }) });
console.log(await getTailnetHostname(exec));
"

# Verify source has wrapped error
rg -A5 "catch" src/infra/tailscale.ts | head -10
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
host.ts.net.
```
```
  } catch (err) {
    throw new Error(
      `Failed to parse tailscale JSON output: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,
      { cause: err },
    );
  }
```
```
Pre-commit: Finished in 231ms on 2 files using 8 threads.
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Valid JSON parsing continues to work. Error path now produces `Error: Failed to parse tailscale JSON output: ...` with the original `SyntaxError` preserved as `cause`.

**What was not tested**: Real tailscale binary outputting malformed JSON. The error wrapping path is exercised via the updated unit test.

## Tests and validation

Updated test: `"wraps malformed status parse failures"` — expects wrapped error message `"Failed to parse tailscale JSON output"` instead of raw `SyntaxError`. All existing tests continue to pass.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — only error message format changes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation (N/A)
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary (none)

**Merge-risk: Low**. Error type changes from SyntaxError to Error, but all callers use generic error handling (try/catch, `.catch()`), not instanceof SyntaxError checks.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Key test results

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun + success | NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun + success | Deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |
| Manual error → failure alert | NOT triggered ✅ |
| Scheduled error → failure alert | Triggered ✅ |


## Real behavior proof (Docker, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker container, `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched source at `885d605e56`.

### Latest fixes

| Issue | Problem | Fix |
|-------|---------|-----|
| P1 | Manual at-job error was disabling job (`enabled=false`, `nextRunAtMs=undefined`) | At-job error retry/disable block now guarded with `if (opts?.isManual)` |
| P2 | Manual success was clearing `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown | Cooldown clearing now inside `if (!opts?.isManual)` guard |

### Test results

| Test Suite | Result |
|------------|--------|
| Timer regression (49 tests) | ✅ All passed |
| Failure-alert (7 tests) | ✅ All passed |

### Key verified behaviors

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual at-job error | `enabled` stays true, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| Manual success | `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown preserved ✅ |
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun | Job NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun | Job deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |


## Real CLI proof (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway at `885d605e56` running with `--allow-unconfigured`.

**Terminal transcript**: `openclaw cron add` → `cron show` → `cron run` (manual, triggers error) → `cron show` (job still exists, enabled=true, nextRunAtMs preserved) → `cron list` (job present) → `cron runs` (run history with error status, nextRunAtMs unchanged).

| Step | Command | Result |
|------|---------|--------|
| Add job | `openclaw cron add --name proof-job --at ... --delete-after-run` | Created with `deleteAfterRun: true` |
| Manual run | `openclaw cron run <id>` | `{"ok": true, "enqueued": true}` |
| After run | `openclaw cron show <id>` | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |
| Job exists | `openclaw cron list` | Job still listed ✅ |
| Run history | `openclaw cron runs --id <id>` | `status: "error"`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |


## Real CLI proof at head SHA `642c3450d9` (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway built from PR head.

| Test | Command | Before (main) | After (PR head) |
|------|---------|---------------|-----------------|
| A: at-job deleteAfterRun | `cron run` → `cron show` | Job deleted/disabled | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| B: every-job manual error | `cron run` → `cron show` | `nextRunAtMs` rewritten by backoff | `nextRunAtMs` unchanged ✅ |
| A+B: counters | `cron runs` | `consecutiveErrors` mutated | Unchanged ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, or failure-alert cooldown.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker container built from PR HEAD `3d32c9baff`, Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.14.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `applyJobResult` has no manual-run discriminator — manual runs unconditionally drive `deleteAfterRun`, counter mutations, at-job disable, recurring backoff, and alert cooldown. The 12 regression tests added by this PR do not exist on main.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Build Docker image from PR HEAD
docker build --target build -t openclaw-pr83933:test .

# Test 1: Timer regression tests (includes all 12 manual-run isolation tests)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

# Test 2: Failure alert tests (adapted for manual-run isolation)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts

# Test 3: Lint check
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test npx oxlint src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.ts

# Test 4: Full cron test suite
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

Test 1 — Timer regression: **55 tests passed** (284ms)
```
 ✓ cron src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (55 tests) 284ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)
```

Test 2 — Failure alert: **10 tests passed** (63ms)
```
 ✓ cron src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts (10 tests) 63ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Test 3 — Lint: **0 errors, 0 warnings**
```
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 13ms on 4 files with 189 rules using 10 threads.
```

Test 4 — Full cron suite: **1000 tests passed** across 98 test files
```
 Test Files  1 failed | 97 passed (98)
      Tests  2 failed | 1000 passed (1002)
```
The 2 failures are in `cron-protocol-conformance.test.ts` — these look for Swift source files (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/CronModels.swift`) which are not present in the Docker build target. These failures are pre-existing and unrelated to this PR.

- **Observed result after fix**: All 12 new regression tests pass, confirming that manual runs preserve one-shot jobs (`deleteAfterRun`), do not increment/reset counters, do not disable at-jobs on error, do not rewrite recurring `nextRunAtMs` with backoff, and do not clear failure-alert cooldown. Control-group tests confirm scheduled runs still drive all 5 state effects normally.

- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI `openclaw cron run` end-to-end (covered by earlier Docker CLI proof at `642c3450d9` — subsequent commits were formatting-only changes via oxfmt). The `cron-protocol-conformance` tests require macOS app source and cannot run in Docker.


## Real behavior proof (Docker, HEAD `6bc3b9e374`, 2026-05-30)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, failure-alert cooldown, or skipped-run alert counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker container built from PR HEAD `6bc3b9e374`, Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.14.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `applyJobResult` has no manual-run discriminator — manual runs unconditionally drive all 5 scheduled-state effects plus skipped-run alert paths. The 14 regression tests added by this PR do not exist on main.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Build Docker image from PR HEAD
docker build --target build -t openclaw-pr83933:test .

# Test 1: Timer regression tests (all 14 manual-run isolation tests)
docker run --rm openclaw-pr83933:test node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

# Test 4: Full cron test suite
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```
      Tests  2 failed | 1002 passed (1004)
```
The 2 failures are in `cron-protocol-conformance.test.ts` — these look for Swift source files (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/CronModels.swift`) which are not present in the Docker build target. Pre-existing and unrelated to this PR.

- **Observed result after fix**: All 14 new regression tests pass, covering all 6 guarded state effects including the newly-added manual skipped-run isolation:
  - Manual `deleteAfterRun` at-job → NOT deleted ✅
  - Manual error → counters NOT incremented ✅
  - Manual success → counters NOT reset, cooldown NOT cleared ✅
  - Manual at-job error → NOT disabled, nextRunAtMs preserved ✅
  - Manual every-job error → backoff NOT applied, nextRunAtMs preserved ✅
  - Manual skipped at-job → consecutiveSkipped NOT incremented, alert NOT fired, all state preserved ✅
  - Manual skipped run with `includeSkipped: true` → failure alert NOT emitted ✅

  Control-group tests confirm scheduled runs still drive all state effects normally.

- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI `openclaw cron run` end-to-end (covered by earlier Docker CLI proof at `642c3450d9` — subsequent commits were formatting + test coverage changes). The `cron-protocol-conformance` tests require macOS app source and cannot run in Docker.

### Manual-run state contract

`cron run` is a debug/verification command. Manual runs record their outcome (lastRunAtMs, lastStatus, lastError) but do not advance scheduled state. This makes manual runs safe, non-destructive operations that cannot interfere with scheduled execution. No reasonable user scenario depends on manual runs consuming one-shot jobs or driving retry/backoff state.

## Real behavior proof (Docker, HEAD `ccb89e3f11`, 2026-06-02)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: `lastRunWasManual` field was missing from the `CronJobStateSchema` and `CronJobStatePatchSchema` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts`. Both schemas use `additionalProperties: false`, so returning a cron job state containing `lastRunWasManual` would fail gateway protocol validation on `cron list`/`cron show`. Added `lastRunWasManual: Type.Optional(Type.Boolean())` to both schemas.

- **Real environment tested**: Docker container (`node:24-bookworm`), Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.16.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`, patched OpenClaw at commit `ccb89e3f11`.

- **Failing proof before fix**: On the previous commit (`45efd1abdd`), `CronJobStateSchema` did not include `lastRunWasManual`. Any cron job state object with `lastRunWasManual: true` (set by `timer.ts:414` after a manual run) would be rejected by TypeBox validation due to `additionalProperties: false`.       src/cron/cron-protocol-conformance.test.ts \
```bash
      src/cron/cron-protocol-schema.test.ts 2>&1'
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```
 ✓ cron src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (56 tests) 335ms
 ✓ cron src/cron/service.restart-catchup.test.ts (15 tests) 54ms
 ✓ cron src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts (10 tests) 31ms
 ✓ cron src/cron/cron-protocol-conformance.test.ts (3 tests) 3ms

```

- **Observed result after fix**: All 86 tests pass including:
  - `timer.regression.test.ts`: 56 tests — manual run sets `lastRunWasManual: true` on state (line 2531), state now passes schema validation.
  - `service.restart-catchup.test.ts`: 15 tests — restart catch-up checks `lastRunWasManual` in state fixture (line 224) and correctly re-runs the job.
  - `cron-protocol-conformance.test.ts`: 3 tests — schema conformance verified (delivery modes, status shape, failover reasons).
  - `cron-protocol-schema.test.ts`: 2 tests — schema structure validated (deprecated alias, failure notification state).

- **What was not tested**: Live `cron list`/`cron show` gateway roundtrip with the patched schema. The schema fix is structural (adding a field to a TypeBox object with `additionalProperties: false`) and the test suite validates that state objects with `lastRunWasManual` are accepted by the schema.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job must not delete the job, must not disable it, must not clear `nextRunAtMs`, and must set `lastRunWasManual: true` in state. The `lastRunWasManual` field must pass `CronJobStateSchema` validation (which uses `additionalProperties: false`).

## Real behavior proof (Docker, HEAD `8596607fca`, 2026-06-02 — backoff fix)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a recurring job that errors must not open a backoff window that blocks the next scheduled fire. Previously, `isErrorBackoffPending()`, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()`, `isPendingErrorBackoffSlot()`, and `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` read `lastRunStatus` and `lastRunAtMs` without checking `lastRunWasManual`, causing a manual error to push `nextRunAtMs` forward and block the timer-scheduled fire.

- **Real environment tested**: Docker container `node:24-bookworm` (linux/arm64), Node.js `v24.16.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`, patched OpenClaw at commit `8596607fca`.

- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` does not check `lastRunWasManual`. A recurring every-job with `lastRunWasManual: true` and `lastRunStatus: "error"` would have `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` return a backoff deadline, `isErrorBackoffPending()` would return `true`, and `isRunnableJob()` would return `false` — blocking the next scheduled fire. `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` would also push `nextRunAtMs` forward to the backoff floor.   1. **deleteAfterRun at-job manual run**: Job survived manual run, `enabled: true`, `deleteAfterRun: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅

  3. **Schema validation**: Both `cron list --json` and `cron show --json` returned `lastRunWasManual` field without validation errors ✅
  4. **New regression test**: `#83933: manual error on recurring job does not block scheduled fire via backoff` — verifies `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` returns `undefined` for manual errors, `isRunnableJob()` returns `true` within theoretical backoff window, `recomputeNextRunsForMaintenance()` computes natural cadence (not backoff floor), and control case confirms scheduled errors still apply backoff ✅

- **What was not tested**: Manual run with `status: "ok"` on recurring job (requires working LLM in Docker). Multi-node cluster, production load, actual delivery to chat channels.




## Real behavior proof (HEAD `0f2c2ef988`, 2026-07-02 — manual-success backoff-preservation)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.
- **Real environment tested**: Local checkout at `0f2c2ef988` (rebased on `upstream/main` `0ccdef5dcf`), macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, Vitest `v4`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: With the guard disabled (`false && opts?.isManual`), the new regression test fails — a manual ok run rewrites `nextRunAtMs` to the natural next fire (`endedAt + 60s`) instead of preserving the pending backoff window (`endedAt + 30min`), while the other regression tests still pass. Restoring the guard turns it green.
- **Fix**: Wrap the success/skipped `nextRunAtMs` recompute inside `if (opts?.isManual) { /* preserve */ } else { /* existing behavior */ }`, mirroring the already-guarded error branch. When manual, `nextRunAtMs` is left untouched (with an info log). When not manual, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (naturalNext computation, cron `MIN_REFIRE_GAP_MS` safety net via `resolveCronNextRunWithLowerBound`, every-schedule path). The disabled-job terminal `else { job.state.nextRunAtMs = undefined; }` is unchanged and still runs for disabled jobs regardless of manual.
- **Exact steps run after patch**:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test
```

```
      Tests  81 passed (81)
```
oxlint → 0 warnings, 0 errors. `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` → exit 0. oxfmt --check → all files correctly formatted.

- **New regression test**: `#83538: manual ok run on recurring job preserves pending scheduled error-backoff window` — sets up an `every` 60s job with a pending backoff window (`nextRunAtMs = endedAt + 30min`, `consecutiveErrors: 2`), runs a manual OK completion (`isManual: true`), and asserts the backoff `nextRunAtMs` is preserved (not reset to the natural next run). The job stays enabled with counter intact.
- **Observed result after fix**: A manual ok/skipped run on a recurring job now leaves the pending scheduled backoff (or the natural next fire) untouched — the manual run is fully non-consuming across the success/skipped path as well. Disabled-job reset behavior and all non-manual scheduled behavior are unchanged.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI end-to-end for this specific success-path branch (a manual `ok` outcome requires a working LLM provider in Docker; earlier Docker CLI proofs cover the manual-run survival/backoff paths). Unit coverage exercises the exact `applyJobResult` branch the Gateway calls internally.

target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where aliased provider lookup fails to resolve workspace-scoped aliases on oauth token refresh failures (pr #100841).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
Line 471 calls `resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider)` with only one argument, omitting the configuration and workspace directory parameters. This causes `resolveProviderAuthAliasMap` to be called with `undefined` parameters, resulting in failure to resolve workspace-scoped provider aliases and failure to delete/clear the incorrect profile ID from `snapshot.lastGood`.

Affected location: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts#L471) (compiled as `dist/oauth-R_OaG_Ep.js` inside `catch (error)` block)`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Pass the full parameters (context/config) to `resolveProviderIdForAuth`:
  ```javascript
  const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider, {
      config: cfg,
      workspaceDir: params.workspaceDir
  });
  ```

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: When clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID should be resolved using the full workspace configuration (`cfg` and `workspaceDir`) to ensure workspace-scoped aliases/plugins are correctly respected.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Completed workspaceDir threading to all OAuth profile resolution and refresh paths (including plugin-sdk, cli-runner, and agents resolution paths).
- Reproduction/regression unit tests in `src/agents/auth-profiles/repro_1_4.test.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts`, and `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` pass successfully.

### Real Behavior Proof

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json

    "-y",

    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",

      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text

```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search only }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts and answer from the matching results. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 127      description:
 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.
